Short diagnostic update (initial):
- Correlated timestamps with our telemetry: at 07:48 PST we have a spike in prefix cache miss rate for the hosted routing pool servicing BrightCommerce (route: /generate, model: rwd-open-3b). Miss rate jumped from ~4% to ~52% for a subset of request prefixes.
- Root suspect: a rollout earlier this week changed the "prefix_cache_invalidation" flag in the hosted config to aggressively evict based on TTL and recent heuristics. That change appears to have combined with a cold-start wave on a set of shards -> significantly more KV lookups and longer KV warmups (extra 1.4s median on some calls).
- Error increase likely tied to backend timeouts that cascade when the KV warmups push token latency past gateway thresholds.

Immediate mitigations I'm executing now:
1) Rolling back the prefix_cache_invalidation experiment in the hosted config to the previous conservative policy (expect effect within ~3m after config propagate).
2) Enabling fast fallback routing for BrightCommerce to the "latency-optimized" model variant (rwd-open-3b-lt) for 5m to shed load from affected shards.
3) Triggering a targeted pre-warm job for affected model shards in us-west-2 (small batch of synthetic warm requests) to rebuild KV entries.
4) Increasing gateway timeout to 6s for the route to reduce 504s while we stabilize (short window).

I'll post telemetry in 10 minutes. Attaching p95/p99 chart and raw error snippets.

-- Dylan
